fieldMarks: Adult male: unmistakably colourful for most of the year.
Female: hint of a crest, dark back and a white eye-patch on a grey head.
Eclipse male resembles the female but with a more distinct white throat.
In flight looks long-tailed and dark, with a white trailing edge on the inner wing.
behavior: Nests in large tree cavities near water, up to about 20 m (65 ft) high, and readily uses nest boxes.
Pairs form on the wintering grounds; northern birds migrate while southern females may be resident.
Feeds from the surface, by dipping its head or on land; acorns are a major food in many areas, plus seeds, waste grain and invertebrates.
habitat: Shallow inland lakes, ponds, slow rivers and swamps surrounded by deciduous or mixed woodland, often where large trees overhang the water; also open marshes within forested country.
range: Breeds across southern Canada and much of the United States, most abundant in the East, with northern birds migrating south; appears to be expanding its range north and west.

lookalikes.name: Mandarin duck
lookalikes.howToTell: Audubon notes the mandarin duck of eastern Asia is the wood duck's only close relative.
